skill_tags: Complex Polar Form and De Moivre's Theorem

hints: Determine the argument $\theta$ in the third quadrant ($-\pi < \theta \leqslant \pi$).
walkthrough:
Determine the principal argument $\theta = \arg(u)$. Since $\operatorname{Re}(u) = -1 < 0$ and $\operatorname{Im}(u) = -\sqrt{3} < 0$, $u$ lies in the third quadrant:
$$\theta = -\pi + \arctan\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1}\right) = -\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$$

State $u$ in exact polar trigonometric form $r(\cos\theta + \mathrm{i}\sin\theta)$:
$$u = 2\left[\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right]$$

skill_tags: Complex Polar Form and De Moivre's Theorem

hints: Calculate the modulus of the quotient: $|v/u| = \dfrac{|v|}{|u|} = \dfrac{5}{2}$.
Calculate the argument of the quotient: $\arg(v/u) = \arg(v) - \arg(u) = \dfrac{\pi}{6} - \left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$.
walkthrough:
Find the modulus $R$ of the quotient $\dfrac{v}{u}$ using $|v| = 5$ and $|u| = 2$:
$$R = \left|\dfrac{v}{u}\right| = \dfrac{|v|}{|u|} = \dfrac{5}{2}$$

Find the argument of the quotient using $\arg(v) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\arg(u) = -\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$:
$$\theta = \arg(v) - \arg(u) = \dfrac{\pi}{6} - \left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{4\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$$
Since $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ lies in the principal range $(-\pi, \pi]$, no interval adjustment is needed.

Express $\dfrac{v}{u}$ in the required exponential form $R\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\theta}$:
$$\dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{5}{2}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5}{6}\pi\mathrm{i}} \quad \left(\text{or } \dfrac{5}{2}\mathrm{e}^{5\pi\mathrm{i}/6}\right)$$
